clue.text: Musical talent a stallholder yearns for

definitions.meaning: the gift of naming any note heard without a reference tone
a market trader wants the ideal spot to set up a stall, a flawless place to pitch

explanation.surface: A market trader dreams of having a musician's gift.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'pitch' as a trader's patch of ground in a market, and the best one is what every stallholder wants.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute recognition of musical notes by ear is the rare gift known by this phrase.

clue.text: Party leader uplifted when paid tribute

indicators.note: the leader of the word Party is its opening letter

parts.note: uplifted means raised, lifted higher

explanation.surface: A political chief is buoyed up by the compliments paid to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifted' looks like a reversal signal in a down clue, but it is simply the synonym RAISED after P.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise someone is to honour them in words, which is paying tribute.

clue.text: After relaxation I have become uneasy

indicators.note: after says the second piece follows the first, as the clue's order shows

parts.note: relaxation is rest
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone finds that taking a break has only made them fidgety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I have' becomes IVE as in the contraction I've, with its apostrophe dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Restive describes someone fidgety and unable to settle, which is being uneasy.

clue.text: English capitalist finds purpose in Church festival

indicators.note: in says one word sits within the other

parts.note: Easter is a major festival of the Christian Church
a purpose is an end, an aim

explanation.surface: An English financier discovers his true calling at Easter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capitalist' is not a financier: it is a person from the capital, London. The East End is a district of east London, so an EAST ENDER lives there.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident of London's East End is a dweller in England's capital, playfully a 'capitalist'.

clue.text: Quality paintings are shown up by it

indicators.note: in a down clue, shown up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: paintings are art
taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic says the paintings' merit is exposed by some object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown up' is a down-clue reversal signal; the surface reads it as paintings being exposed or outclassed.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait is a distinguishing characteristic, one of a person's qualities.

clue.text: Bearing flowers for stylish British weaver

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
a loom is the machine that weaves cloth

explanation.surface: A fashionable British textile worker is offered as the reason for a flowery display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weaver' looks like a person, but it is the machine, LOOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant in bloom has its blossoms open, so it is bearing flowers.

clue.text: Batter one's belongings

definitions.meaning: to batter is to beat someone hard
in British slang, a person's stuff or gear

explanation.surface: A thug beats a victim and takes his things.
explanation.walkthrough: Clobber is everyday British slang both for hitting someone and for one's clothes and possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are British slang: thump hard, and personal gear or kit.

clue.text: College gains a minor acting trophy

parts.note: an academy is a college or school
taken as written
a ward is a minor placed under a guardian's care

explanation.surface: A drama school takes on a young actor who goes on to win a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minor' looks like an adjective, but it is a noun: a child in someone's legal care, a WARD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oscar, the film industry's famous statuette for performers, is formally called this.

clue.text: Many girls in tuition groups

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: Lots of young women attend lessons together.
explanation.definitionFit: A school's teaching is organised into sets of pupils taught together.

clue.text: A physician was promoted by saintly bishop

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
someone who was promoted rose in rank

explanation.surface: A doctor's advancement comes thanks to a holy churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: St Ambrose was the fourth-century Bishop of Milan.
explanation.definitionFit: St Ambrose was Bishop of Milan and is honoured as a saint and Doctor of the Church.

clue.text: Lover's gift to atone for all-time ding-dong?

parts.note: all time without end is eternity
the ding-dong of a bell is its ring

explanation.surface: A lover buys a present to make up for the biggest row ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ding-dong' is British slang for a quarrel, which is why a gift to atone for one fits the surface; in the wordplay it is the sound of a bell, RING. 'to atone for' joins the halves.
explanation.definitionFit: A band set with a continuous circle of stones is given as a token of everlasting love.

clue.text: Journalist taken aback by malice, notwithstanding

indicators.note: taken aback means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword's usual journalist
malice is spite

explanation.surface: A reporter is startled by someone's spite but carries on regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' looks like surprise, but it turns ED backwards to DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Despite and notwithstanding are synonyms, both meaning in spite of.

clue.text: After brief time Russian currency is in difficulty

indicators.note: after puts the currency behind the abbreviation for time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
the rouble is the currency of Russia

explanation.surface: Shortly afterwards, Russia's money gets into a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief time' is the abbreviation T, not a short period; ROUBLE comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in trouble is being in difficulty: the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Forced to accommodate good woman

indicators.note: to accommodate is to take in, so one word holds the other

parts.note: made, as in 'made him go', means forced

explanation.surface: A virtuous woman is compelled to put someone up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good woman' looks like one phrase, but 'good' gives G and 'woman' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Madge is a woman's name, a pet form of Margaret.

clue.text: Strange dream once related by Boccaccio

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters are made odd, rearranged

explanation.surface: A peculiar dream that a famous Italian writer once recounted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges DREAM ONCE. 'related' means told, so the definition is the thing Boccaccio told.
explanation.definitionFit: The Decameron is Boccaccio's fourteenth-century collection of a hundred tales, the stories he narrated.

clue.text: Church design Stella and I regarded as heavenly

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: to design something is to arrange it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A church whose design two people consider divine.
explanation.walkthrough: The text as held lost the I the anagram needs; 'design' is the anagram signal, mixing up the name Stella with I, and 'regarded as' joins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Celestial and heavenly both describe what belongs to the sky or to paradise.

clue.text: Inherited by constituents of Lancaster

indicators.note: the constituents of a word are its letters, here taken in a new order

explanation.surface: Something passed down via the voters of a northern city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' looks like voters in Lancaster's constituency, but it means the letters of the word, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: What is ancestral has come down from forebears, as an inheritance does.

clue.text: Present-day electricity charge

definitions.meaning: a flow of electric charge through a conductor

explanation.surface: The modern bill for one's power supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like a bill, but it is electric charge, whose flow is the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both 'happening now' and 'a flow of electricity'.

clue.text: Various changes wrought by the Messiah

indicators.note: changes says the letters undergo alteration into a new order

explanation.surface: Many transformations brought about by Christ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges VARIOUS; 'wrought by' joins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Christians call Christ, the promised deliverer, the Saviour.

clue.text: Should need nothing

definitions.meaning: the verb meaning must, as in 'you should go'
as a noun, an obligation or duty

explanation.surface: A claim that one is obliged to want for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Three senses: the verb 'should', the noun for an obligation, and the old word for zero.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a duty, the modal verb of obligation, and also zero as in nought.

clue.text: Silver in bizarre setting causes grave offence

indicators.note: a setting surrounds a jewel, so one word holds the other

parts.note: outré means bizarre or unconventional
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A jeweller's odd mount for a silver piece causes great upset.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text splits 'setting' in two. Outré is a French-derived word for outlandish; a jewel's setting holds the silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Outrage is a deeply offensive act, or the indignation it causes.

clue.text: Sauces I discovered in tombs

indicators.note: something discovered in a place is found inside it

parts.note: graves are tombs

explanation.surface: An archaeologist finds condiments in burial sites.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravy is a meat sauce, so gravies are sauces.

clue.text: Coming from Arkansas with another competitor

parts.note: AR is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Arkansas
a rival is another competitor

explanation.surface: Another contestant comes in from Arkansas.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrival, as a noun, is the act of coming to a place.

clue.text: Inclination expressed by composer

indicators.note: expressed means spoken, so the word is heard as it sounds

parts.note: a list is a lean or tilt, especially of a ship

explanation.surface: A preference voiced by a famous musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclination' looks like a liking, but it is a ship's lean, LIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a nineteenth-century Hungarian pianist and composer.

clue.text: Established carnival likely to succeed

parts.note: something established is set, fixed
a fair is a carnival or funfair

explanation.surface: A long-running carnival seems bound to do well.
explanation.walkthrough: Set fair is a barometer reading for settled weather, hence a good outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Set fair means in a favourable position, poised for success.

clue.text: Guardian spirits made son reform

indicators.note: reform means form again, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Protective spirits caused a boy to mend his ways.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek belief a daemon is an attendant spirit watching over a person.

clue.text: I translated a Latin language

indicators.note: translated means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone renders a Latin text into a modern tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian is the Romance tongue spoken in Italy.

clue.text: Liars with novel ideas

definitions.meaning: people who come up with fiction, writers of novels and tales

explanation.surface: Fibbers who think up new notions.
explanation.walkthrough: A teller of stories can be a fibber or an author of fiction; 'novel' points to the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both fibbers and narrators of fiction such as novelists.
